title: Decompose legacy entity materialized views and introduce partial indexes to reduce control-plane join hotspots
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: The control plane currently relies on two large legacy materialized views (entity_join_mv, audit_join_mv) that perform wide joins across users, tenants, and audit_event JSONB payloads. These views are causing frequent sequential scans and expensive join plans for common read paths (route listing, audit queries). This ticket decomposes the views into targeted, narrow tables and adds predicate-driven partial indexes and covering indexes for the hot queries. The goal is: 1) reduce p95 read latency for list endpoints by 30-60%, 2) reduce DB CPU for query slices by ~40% under load, and 3) simplify future schema migrations by normalizing frequently-filtered JSONB keys into columns.
acceptance_criteria: Decompose entity_join_mv into entity_lookup and entity_metadata (normalized columns for tenant_id, status, last_active_at)
Replace audit_join_mv with audit_events_flat where commonly-filtered JSONB keys are moved into columns and other payloads remain in jsonb payload column
Add partial indexes for (tenant_id, status) and a covering index for (tenant_id, created_at DESC) matching the top 5 query patterns
Benchmarked improvement: p95 latency for /routes endpoint reduced by >=30% in staging (same dataset as production snapshot)
Migration SQLs included and runbook validated with dry-run on staging; zero-downtime rollback path documented
Code review approvals and DB migration applied in canary region with monitoring dashboards showing expected metrics
migration_steps: Create new narrow tables (entity_lookup, entity_metadata, audit_events_flat) with minimal constraints and no triggers in staging
Backfill entity_lookup and entity_metadata from current materialized views using batched INSERT ... SELECT (batch size 5k) with progress logging
Add partial indexes on production-readable predicates but concurrently (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY) to avoid locking
Switch read paths in application: add feature flag for new lookup table; keep old views for writes until verification
Run integration tests and perf harness against staging snapshot dataset (2026-02-20 production export)
Rollout to canary region then globally using phased feature flag (10% -> 50% -> 100%)
Once stable for 48 hours, schedule a maintenance migration to drop legacy materialized views and any obsolete columns
Update observability: add new Grafana panels for index hit ratio and plan changes; add slow-query alerts for new tables
rollback_plan: If regressions observed during canary (latency increase >10% or error rate >0.5%), flip feature flag to old views and revert to previous read plan. For partially applied migrations, run targeted DELETEs/RE-INSERTs to restore previous consistent state from materialized view copies created pre-migration. If index creation causes unexpected IO, DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY in canary region and pause rollout. All rollback actions must be coordinated with DB operations and SRE on-call.
comments: 2026-02-14 Maya Chen: Spike complete. Staging runs show 35-48% reduction in p95 for /routes with new entity_lookup table and partial indexes. Query plans moved from nested loop + seqscan to index scan + top-n heap fetch.

2026-02-25 Code review (PR 2284): Requested adding unit test for JSONB migration edge-case where payload->>'status' is null; addressed with COALESCE in backfill SQL.
2026-03-01 Perf team: Ran heavy-load synthetic test (1000 rps) against staging snapshot. Observed 42% CPU reduction for control-plane read worker; p99 unchanged. Approved canary rollout.
2026-03-08 Liam O'Connor: Canary region rollout started at 10%. Monitoring shows expected improvements; no errors. Will proceed to 50% tomorrow unless SRE flags an issue.
